description: request-wallet-sign is a standalone npm CLI utility that lets AI agents request wallet signatures from a human through a browser interface without ever holding private keys. The agent passes transaction details as command-line arguments and the tool spins up a local server that displays a decoded, plain-English summary of the request, where the user connects a wallet, reviews the details, and approves the signing. It runs local-only by default for instant use, supports standard transactions, typed data, and personal signatures, and can use Cloudflare tunnels for cross-device signing, with a built-in timeout that auto-closes tabs once a request is handled.

name: Base MCP
description: Base MCP is a Model Context Protocol server that connects AI agents to wallet and onchain tools on Base, with pre-built prompts and workflows for wallet operations, token transfers, and DeFi interactions. Nothing happens onchain without explicit approval since the server never holds or accesses private keys, instead constructing pending requests that a Base Account reviews and signs, and it ships with skill plugins covering Morpho, Moonwell, Aerodrome, Bankr, Avantis, Virtuals, and Uniswap.

name: WalletChan MCP
description: WalletChan MCP is a local MCP adapter that connects AI agents to WalletChan wallet accounts through popup approvals, portfolio reads, swaps, and bridges, with optional delegated execution via ERC-7710 permissions. It lets local MCP clients like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Codex interact with a WalletChan wallet across Base, Ethereum, Polygon, and Unichain.

name: Morpho Agents
description: Morpho Agents is a beta interface built for AI agents to read, simulate, and write to Morpho's lending protocols. The User Agent product is a CLI and MCP server giving agents full read, simulate, and write access on Ethereum and Base with any wallet infrastructure, running every write through a simulation first, while the Builder Agent is an AGENTS.md knowledge base that turns a code agent into a Morpho integration expert.

name: Pendle AI
description: Pendle AI is a set of AI plugins for Pendle Finance, packaged as MCP servers, that let agents trade yield tokens, manage LP positions, place limit orders, and query DeFi market data across seven EVM chains. It includes a Pendle V2 plugin for the core yield-trading protocol and a Boros plugin for interest-rate derivatives on Arbitrum, and is compatible with Claude Code and other MCP-based tools.

name: Across Skills
description: Across Skills is a knowledge base and MCP endpoint for building crosschain applications on Across, covering the Across swap API, suggested fees, deposit tracking, and embedded crosschain actions that execute contract calls across different chains in a single transaction. It is aimed at both AI agents and developers building production crosschain apps, and is available under an MIT license.

name: OpenSea Skills
description: OpenSea Skills is a collection of agent skills for interacting with the OpenSea NFT marketplace, bundled under a router skill that directs an agent to the right sub-skill for its task. It covers querying NFT and collection data, buying and selling items through the Seaport protocol, swapping ERC20 tokens, configuring wallet signers, and registering gated AI tools, and installs via the Agent Skills spec with npx skills add.

name: Bitrefill Skill
description: Bitrefill Skill is an agent skill that routes an AI assistant through buying gift cards, mobile top-ups, and eSIMs from Bitrefill across 180-plus countries and 1,500-plus brands, paid for with crypto, Lightning, USDC, or a prefunded Bitrefill balance. It detects the execution environment and available wallet integrations to pick the lowest-friction checkout path, supports guest checkout via Base wallet sign-in, and keeps user-facing messaging free of technical jargon like x402, MCP, or JWT.

name: Bankr Skills
description: Bankr Skills is a catalog of plug-and-play agent skills built around Bankr's wallet, trading, and security infrastructure, letting builders add natural-language crypto trading, portfolio management, token launching, and DeFi operations to an agent without standing up wallet plumbing themselves. Specialized skills in the catalog cover things like deploying ERC-20 tokens with Uniswap V4 pools, cross-chain swaps across 50-plus chains via Symbiosis, and prediction-market intelligence, all routable from natural language across Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Solana, and Unichain.

name: CoinGecko MCP
description: CoinGecko MCP is a remote Model Context Protocol server that gives AI agents access to CoinGecko's market data, including live prices and market caps, historical charts, DeFi and onchain pool data, and NFT collection analytics. It connects to Claude, Cursor, VS Code, and other MCP clients with minimal setup and is backed by CoinGecko's existing API.

name: Tenderly MCP
description: Tenderly MCP is a Model Context Protocol server that brings Tenderly's blockchain development tools into AI assistants like Claude, exposing around 59 tools for transaction simulation, virtual testing environments, call trace and event inspection, and project management. It authenticates via OAuth and lets an agent set an active project, then run simulations and debug transactions without leaving the chat.

name: DefiLlama Skills
description: DefiLlama Skills is a collection of MCP skills exposing roughly 23 DeFi analytics tools built on DefiLlama data, covering full market snapshots of TVL, categories, chains, events, and stablecoins alongside guided workflows for protocol analysis, token research, chain ecosystem comparisons, yield strategy discovery, and risk assessment. It is aimed specifically at wiring DefiLlama's analytics into AI agents, distinct from the main DefiLlama analytics site.

name: Envio
description: Envio is a multichain indexing framework with TypeScript, JavaScript, or ReScript handlers that syncs over HyperSync rather than RPC when you need one Postgres-backed GraphQL API across several EVM chains.

name: dRPC
description: dRPC is a hosted RPC service that spreads JSON-RPC, WebSocket, and REST traffic across independent node providers on Ethereum, its L2s, and 200+ other networks. It covers archive data, MEV-protected transaction endpoints, per-key rate limits, and usage dashboards, so reach for it when you want managed endpoints with provider redundancy instead of running nodes yourself.

name: NodeCore
description: NodeCore is a self-hosted RPC load balancer in Go that sits in front of several blockchain API providers and scores upstreams on latency, error rate, and availability to pick one per request. It layers caching, request hedging, retries, per-method rate limiting, and quorum verification over JSON-RPC, WebSocket, and REST interfaces, so reach for it when you run your own RPC cluster and want failover across providers rather than a single endpoint.

name: EVM RPC Picker
description: A terminal UI that searches 1000+ EVM chains, latency-tests their public RPC endpoints, and exports the winner as ETH_RPC_URL for Foundry and Hardhat commands. It also manages your own private endpoints with encrypted storage and per-project favorites, so reach for it when you switch chains often and are tired of pasting RPC URLs.

name: Wake
description: Wake is a Python framework for testing, fuzzing, and static analysis of Solidity projects. Builders reach for it when they want to write contract tests and fuzzing campaigns in Python and run analysis over the same codebase.

name: Huff
description: Huff is a low-level assembly language and compiler for writing hand-optimized EVM bytecode, with development continuing in huff2. Builders reach for it when bytecode has to be tuned by hand.

name: ABDKMath64x64
description: ABDKMath64x64 is a Solidity library for 64.64-bit binary fixed-point math. Builders import it when a contract needs fixed-point arithmetic that Solidity does not provide natively.

name: ERC721A
description: ERC721A is a gas-optimized ERC-721 implementation with cheap consecutive batch minting. Builders import it when an NFT contract mints several tokens to the same address at once and minting cost matters.

name: ERC721A-Upgradeable
description: ERC721A-Upgradeable is the proxy-upgradeable variant of the ERC721A implementation. Builders import it when a proxy-based NFT contract needs the batch minting design of ERC721A.

name: Safe Smart Account (Gnosis Safe)
description: Safe Smart Account is the widely deployed set of modular multisig smart-account contracts behind Safe. Wallet and treasury builders deploy or extend it to add multisignature control and account modules.

name: Multicall3
description: Multicall3 is the canonical contract for batching many reads or writes into a single transaction. Builders call it from contracts and scripts to fetch or update state across several contracts in one round trip.

name: RainbowKit
description: RainbowKit is a customizable React wallet-connection interface built on wagmi. React builders add it when an application needs a ready-made connect flow instead of wiring wallet selection by hand.

name: Reown AppKit (ex-Web3Modal/WalletConnect SDK)
description: Reown AppKit, formerly Web3Modal and the WalletConnect SDK, is a wallet-connection SDK with a hosted relay, support for over 700 wallets, and embedded logins. Application builders use it to cover both external wallets and embedded sign-in from one integration.

name: ConnectKit
description: ConnectKit provides React wallet-connection components built on wagmi. React builders drop it in when they want prebuilt connect buttons and modals for an application.

name: ethereumjs (monorepo)
description: The ethereumjs monorepo holds core JavaScript primitives for Ethereum, including transaction signing, an EVM implementation, RLP encoding, tries, and shared utilities. JavaScript builders import individual packages when they need protocol-level pieces rather than a full client library.

name: go-ethereum (ethclient/accounts/abigen)
description: go-ethereum ships Go packages for Ethereum development, including the ethclient RPC client, account and key handling, and abigen for type-safe contract bindings. Go builders import them to talk to nodes and call contracts from generated code.

name: ZeroDev SDK (Kernel)
description: The ZeroDev SDK is a smart-account SDK for the Kernel account with modular validators and session keys. Account-abstraction builders use it to create Kernel accounts and delegate limited signing rights to sessions.

name: Biconomy SDK (Nexus)
description: The Biconomy SDK, published as AbstractJS for the Nexus account, builds ERC-4337 smart accounts with paymaster and bundler services. Builders use it when an application needs sponsored or gasless transactions.

name: Safe Protocol Kit (safe-core-sdk)
description: Safe Protocol Kit is the TypeScript SDK of safe-core-sdk for building, signing, and executing Safe multisignature transactions. Builders use it to drive Safe accounts from application or script code.

name: OnchainKit
description: OnchainKit is a set of React components from Coinbase for wallets, transactions, identity, and other onchain interfaces. React builders use it to assemble an onchain frontend from prebuilt pieces.

name: Nethermind
description: Nethermind is an Ethereum execution client written in C# and .NET, and the second most used client on the network. Node operators and infrastructure builders run it to serve JSON-RPC and follow the chain.

name: Besu
description: Besu is a Java Ethereum execution client hosted by LF Decentralized Trust, formerly under Hyperledger, with wide enterprise use. Node operators run it when a deployment is standardized on the Java stack.

name: Erigon
description: Erigon is an efficiency-focused Ethereum execution client that embeds the Caplin consensus layer. Infrastructure builders run it when they want one process for execution and consensus and fast access to historical state.

name: Reth
description: Reth is a modular Ethereum execution client written in Rust by Paradigm. Rust builders run it as a node or extend its components to build custom infrastructure.

name: ethrex
description: ethrex is a minimalist Ethereum execution client written in Rust by LambdaClass with growing adoption. Rust builders run it when they want a compact client codebase to operate or read.

name: Lighthouse
description: Lighthouse is an Ethereum consensus client written in Rust by Sigma Prime and one of the most used clients on the network. Validator and node operators run it to follow and attest to the beacon chain.

name: Prysm
description: Prysm is an Ethereum consensus client written in Go by Prysmatic Labs and historically the most used client. Validator and node operators run it to take part in consensus.

name: Teku
description: Teku is a Java Ethereum consensus client from Consensys that is favored by institutional operators. Validator and node operators run it when a deployment is standardized on the Java stack.

name: Nimbus
description: Nimbus is a resource-efficient Ethereum consensus client written in Nim for low-power hardware. Validator operators run it on small machines where memory and CPU headroom are limited.

name: Lodestar
description: Lodestar is an Ethereum consensus client written in TypeScript by ChainSafe that adds client diversity in the JavaScript ecosystem. TypeScript infrastructure builders run it as a node or reuse its libraries.

name: Grandine
description: Grandine is a multithreaded Ethereum consensus client written in Rust for high throughput. Node operators run it when they want to drive many validators from one process.

name: Ream
description: Ream is a Rust consensus client for the Beam chain, the planned next design of Ethereum consensus. It is under active development and not yet a production option for node operators.

name: QuickNode
description: QuickNode is a hosted RPC provider covering many chains, with an add-on marketplace and service level agreements. Builders subscribe when they want managed endpoints and extra infrastructure services instead of running nodes.

name: Ankr
description: Ankr offers free public and paid RPC endpoints across many chains. Builders point applications at Ankr for hosted chain access without operating their own nodes.

name: Chainstack
description: Chainstack provides managed node and RPC infrastructure with global request routing. Builders use it when an application needs dedicated nodes and endpoints served close to its users.

name: Blockdaemon
description: Blockdaemon runs enterprise node infrastructure together with staking systems and RPC APIs. Infrastructure teams use it when node operation and staking are outsourced under an enterprise agreement.

name: GetBlock
description: GetBlock gives hosted access to nodes on many chains through RPC endpoints. Builders connect applications to it for chain access without running their own infrastructure.

name: Pocket Network (Grove)
description: Pocket Network, served through Grove, is a decentralized RPC relay network with an onchain incentive protocol. Builders use its endpoint network when they want chain access that does not depend on a single provider.

name: PublicNode (Allnodes)
description: PublicNode from Allnodes serves free Ethereum RPC endpoints that need no API key. Builders use it for quick reads, scripts, and fallback endpoints.

name: Tenderly
description: Tenderly provides transaction simulation, trace debugging, alerting, and Virtual TestNets for contracts. Builders use it to replay a failing transaction, watch deployed contracts, and test against a forked network.

name: Routescan
description: Routescan is a multi-chain block explorer with an Etherscan-compatible API. Builders use it to verify contracts and query chain data on networks through the same API calls they already write for Etherscan.

name: beaconcha.in
description: beaconcha.in is an open-source explorer for the Ethereum beacon chain and its validators. Staking and infrastructure builders use it to inspect validator performance and query beacon-chain data.

name: The Graph
description: The Graph is a decentralized indexing protocol where builders deploy subgraphs and query them over GraphQL. Builders use it to turn contract events into a queryable API without running their own indexer.

name: Covalent (GoldRush)
description: Covalent, delivered as GoldRush, is a unified REST API for historical onchain data across many chains. Builders call it when an application needs normalized balances, transfers, and history without writing a chain-specific indexer.

name: Moralis
description: Moralis offers web3 data APIs together with webhook-first event streams. Builders call its REST endpoints for wallet, token, NFT, and price data on Ethereum mainnet and subscribe to Streams webhooks for events.

name: Dune
description: Dune is a community analytics platform where onchain data is queried with SQL and shared as dashboards. Builders write queries or call the API when they need protocol metrics and want to reuse work others have published.

name: Bitquery
description: Bitquery serves decoded blockchain data across networks through GraphQL, Kafka, and gRPC interfaces. Builders use it when an application needs decoded transactions and events from several chains in one place.

name: Nansen
description: Nansen provides onchain analytics with wallet labels and its Smart Money views of what labeled wallets are doing.

name: Subsquid (SQD)
description: Subsquid, also called SQD, is a modular batch indexing SDK backed by distributed data archives. Builders use it to write custom indexers that read from archives instead of pulling every block from an RPC node.

name: SubQuery
description: SubQuery is an open indexing SDK paired with a decentralized network of RPC and indexer operators. Builders define an indexer with it and serve the results as an API.

name: Goldsky
description: Goldsky runs hosted subgraphs and streaming pipelines for onchain data. Builders use it when they want subgraphs and data streams operated for them rather than self-hosted.

name: Substreams
description: Substreams is a parallelized streaming data engine for blockchain data built on Firehose. Data builders write Substreams modules when a pipeline needs to process large ranges of blocks in parallel.

name: Firehose (firehose-ethereum)
description: Firehose, in its firehose-ethereum form, is the flat-file block extraction layer that feeds Substreams. Its documentation addresses operators running a full indexing stack, since Substreams users can reach the same data through hosted endpoints.

name: ethereum-etl
description: ethereum-etl is a Python tool that exports Ethereum data into files and data warehouses. Data builders run it to move blocks, transactions, and logs into their own analytics storage.

name: Shovel
description: Shovel is a configuration-driven tool that indexes EVM logs into PostgreSQL. Builders point it at contracts and tables when they want event data in their own database without writing indexer code.

name: Apibara
description: Apibara builds streaming onchain data pipelines that handle chain reorganizations. Builders use it when a service consumes live chain data and must correct itself when blocks are reorged.

name: TrueBlocks (chifra)
description: TrueBlocks, used through its chifra command, builds a local address-based index on top of an Ethereum node. Builders run it to index and query the full activity of an address from their own machine.

name: Allium
description: Allium is a managed data warehouse and API service for onchain data aimed at institutional use. Builders use it when they want onchain datasets delivered into their analytics stack rather than indexed in house.

name: Chainbase
description: Chainbase is a hosted multi-chain data warehouse with indexing APIs. Builders query it for chain data across networks without operating indexers.

name: Space and Time
description: Space and Time is a SQL data warehouse that produces proofs of its query results for onchain use. Builders query it when a contract or application must trust a computed result rather than a plain API response.

name: Token Terminal
description: Token Terminal publishes standardized financial metrics and dashboards for protocols, such as revenue, fees and active users.

name: Artemis
description: Artemis provides cross-chain fundamentals and metrics dashboards, with an API that serves the same data.

name: Echidna
description: Echidna is a property-based and grammar fuzzer for Ethereum smart contracts. Builders and auditors write properties with it to find inputs that break contract invariants.

name: ItyFuzz
description: ItyFuzz is a bytecode-level smart-contract fuzzer that combines fuzzing with symbolic analysis. Builders and auditors run it against EVM bytecode when source-level fuzzing is not enough or no source is available.

name: Certora Prover
description: Certora Prover is a cloud formal-verification service that checks specifications written in CVL against deployed contract code. Verification engineers use it to prove that a contract holds stated properties for all inputs.

name: Semgrep (smart-contracts rules)
description: Semgrep is a pattern-based static analysis tool with rulesets for Solidity vulnerabilities. Builders run those rules over a codebase to catch known vulnerable patterns and style issues before review.

name: eth-infinitism account-abstraction (SimpleAccount + SDK)
description: The eth-infinitism account-abstraction repository holds the reference ERC-4337 contracts, including SimpleAccount, plus a TypeScript SDK from the authors of the specification. Builders use it as the baseline implementation when creating ERC-4337 accounts.

name: Alto (Pimlico)
description: Alto is a TypeScript ERC-4337 bundler from Pimlico that also runs behind their hosted service. Infrastructure builders run it themselves when they need to operate a bundler instead of relying on a third party.

name: permissionless.js (Pimlico)
description: permissionless.js from Pimlico is a vendor-neutral TypeScript library built on viem for ERC-4337 accounts. TypeScript builders use it to assemble and submit user operations while keeping the choice of bundler and paymaster open.

name: Kernel (ZeroDev)
description: Kernel from ZeroDev is a modular ERC-7579 smart-account contract with wide deployment. Wallet builders deploy it when an account needs pluggable validators and executors.

name: Nexus (Biconomy)
description: Nexus from Biconomy is a modular ERC-7579 smart-account contract aimed at high-volume applications. Wallet builders deploy it as the account implementation behind their smart wallets.

name: Safe 4337 module (safe-modules)
description: The Safe 4337 module adds native ERC-4337 support to Safe multisig accounts. Safe builders install it so an existing multisig can be driven by user operations through a bundler.

name: safe7579 (Rhinestone)
description: safe7579 from Rhinestone is an adapter that makes Safe accounts ERC-7579 compliant. Builders add it when they want portable ERC-7579 modules to run on a Safe, usually alongside the Safe 4337 module.

name: Alchemy aa-sdk / Account Kit
description: Alchemy aa-sdk, shipped as Account Kit, is a full-stack smart wallet SDK with embedded wallets and a gas manager. Application builders use it to give users an account and sponsored transactions without a separate wallet app.

name: Coinbase Smart Wallet
description: Coinbase Smart Wallet is a passkey-based smart account with the largest share of deployed wallets. Application builders integrate it so users sign with a passkey instead of managing a seed phrase.

name: Arka (Etherspot paymaster)
description: Arka is the open-source paymaster service from Etherspot for sponsoring transaction gas. Builders self-host it when gas sponsorship for ERC-4337 accounts should run on their own infrastructure.

name: Rhinestone ModuleKit
description: Rhinestone ModuleKit is a Solidity framework for building and testing ERC-7579 modules. Builders use it when writing validators, executors, or hooks for modular smart accounts.

name: Particle Network
description: Particle Network is a hosted wallet-abstraction stack that bundles a bundler, paymaster, and social login. Builders choose it when they want account creation, login, and transaction sponsorship from one service.

name: hardhat-deploy
description: hardhat-deploy is a Hardhat plugin for replicable deployments with named accounts, proxies, and diamonds. Builders install it when deployments must be repeatable across networks and track upgradeable contracts.

name: Forta
description: Forta is a decentralized network for runtime threat detection and anomaly monitoring. Builders write detection bots and run them on the network to get alerts about suspicious activity against their contracts.

name: Hypernative
description: Hypernative is a hosted platform for real-time onchain threat detection and risk monitoring. Builders choose it when a protocol needs monitored alerts and automated responses to attacks.

name: Safe Transaction Service
description: Safe Transaction Service is the backend that indexes Safe multisig transactions and coordinates their collection of signatures. Safe integrations run or call it to track pending and executed multisig transactions.

name: Web3Signer
description: Web3Signer is a remote signing service that keeps keys in a vault or hardware security module. Node and validator operators run it so signing happens outside the client process.

name: Gelato
description: Gelato is a hosted network that provides a bundler, paymaster and relay for smart accounts together with Web3 Functions for scheduled and event-driven contract execution. Builders use it to run gasless transactions and contract automation without operating those services themselves.

name: abitype
description: abitype provides strict TypeScript types and static inference for Ethereum ABIs, and it is the type layer under viem and wagmi. TypeScript builders import it when contract calls should be checked against the ABI at compile time.

name: web3.swift (Argent)
description: web3.swift from Argent is a Swift library covering Ethereum RPC calls, ABI encoding, and transaction signing. iOS and macOS builders use it to talk to Ethereum from native applications.

name: Fireblocks SDK
description: The Fireblocks SDK drives the Fireblocks MPC custody platform for programmatic signing, transfers, and treasury operations. Builders integrate it when funds are held in Fireblocks custody and movements must be automated.

name: Turnkey
description: Turnkey offers an API and SDK for secure key generation and transaction signing backed by trusted execution environments. Builders use it to create and operate wallet infrastructure without holding raw private keys in their own code.

name: Privy
description: Privy is an embedded self-custodial wallet SDK with progressive authentication and delegated key management. Builders add it so users get a wallet on sign-up and can upgrade to their own custody later.

name: Web3Auth
description: Web3Auth is an MPC and threshold key-management SDK that backs seedless wallets created from a social login. Builders use it when users should sign in with an existing account instead of a seed phrase.

name: Dynamic
description: Dynamic is an SDK covering wallet connection, embedded MPC wallets, and application authentication. Builders choose it when an application must serve both existing wallet users and new users who need one created.

name: Magic (Magic.link)
description: Magic is an embedded non-custodial wallet SDK with email and social login and delegated key management. Builders integrate it to give users a wallet behind a familiar login flow.

name: Sequence (0xsequence)
description: Sequence, published as 0xsequence, is a smart-contract wallet SDK with embedded wallets, a relayer, an indexer, and gasless transactions. Builders use it when a game or application needs wallets and transaction plumbing from one stack.

name: Lit Protocol
description: Lit Protocol is a decentralized network for threshold key management with programmable signing through its programmable key pairs. Builders use its SDK when signing or decryption should follow rules enforced by a network rather than a single key holder.

name: MetaMask Connect
description: MetaMask Connect is the SDK that connects web, mobile and game applications to the MetaMask wallet, replacing the deprecated MetaMask SDK with direct wallet communication and multichain support. Builders install the connect-evm package to reach MetaMask users from any frontend.

name: Coinbase Wallet SDK
description: Coinbase Wallet SDK connects applications to Coinbase Wallet through the injected provider and the mobile WalletLink flow. Builders use it to support Coinbase Wallet users on web and mobile.

name: Web3-Onboard
description: Web3-Onboard is a framework-agnostic wallet-connection library supporting more than 35 wallets and the EIP-1193, 1102, 3085 and 3326 standards, started by Blocknative and now maintained by thirdweb. Builders install it when the frontend is not React or must cover many wallet providers.

name: eth-gas-reporter
description: eth-gas-reporter is a Mocha reporter that prints gas and fiat cost per function call and deployment. Truffle and plain Mocha test suites use it, while Hardhat projects usually pick hardhat-gas-reporter.

name: eth-tester
description: eth-tester is a pluggable in-memory Ethereum backend used by web3.py for fast unit tests. Python builders import it when tests should run against a simulated chain instead of a node.

name: Hive
description: Hive is an end-to-end integration test harness that runs Ethereum clients in Docker across simulator scenarios. Client teams use it to check that implementations agree with each other.

name: Kurtosis ethereum-package
description: The Kurtosis ethereum-package spins up reproducible multi-client Ethereum devnets, including mev-boost and supporting tooling. Builders run it when they need a local network that mirrors a real client mix.

name: sol2uml
description: sol2uml generates UML class and storage-layout diagrams from Solidity source or from verified contracts. Builders run it to see contract relationships and how state variables are packed into storage.

name: heimdall-rs
description: heimdall-rs is a Rust EVM toolkit that disassembles bytecode, decompiles contracts, generates control flow graphs, and decodes calldata and traces. Builders reach for it when they need to understand a contract that has no published source.

name: MEV-Boost
description: MEV-Boost is a validator sidecar that sources blocks from a competitive marketplace of builders and relays under proposer-builder separation. Validator operators run it alongside their consensus client to receive externally built blocks.

name: bloXroute
description: bloXroute is a blockchain distribution network offering low-latency mempool streaming and MEV bundle submission. Builders use it when a trading or infrastructure service needs pending transactions quickly and a path to submit bundles.

name: eth-keys
description: eth-keys is a Python library for secp256k1 keys and signatures, and it sits under eth-account and web3.py. Python builders import it when they need key and signature operations directly.

name: staking-deposit-cli
description: staking-deposit-cli generates validator keys and deposit data for Ethereum staking, and is now maintained as the EthStaker fork that the original owners point to. Validators run it once when setting up new keys.

name: ethdo
description: ethdo is a command line tool for beacon-chain and validator account management, covering keys, withdrawals, and exits. Validator operators use it for one-off account operations outside the client.

name: eth-docker
description: eth-docker is a Dockerized stack for deploying and managing execution, consensus, and validator clients on mainnet. Node operators use it to run a full node setup from configuration files instead of hand-installed binaries.

name: Sentio
description: Sentio is an observability platform combining a transaction debugger, simulation, indexing, metrics, and alerts. Builders use it to trace a failed call and then watch the same contract with dashboards and alerts.

name: recursive calldata decoder
description: A calldata decoder that also unwraps nested function calls. Builders open it when a flat decoder leaves the inner calls of a batched or forwarded transaction unreadable.

name: evm codes
description: evm.codes is an interactive reference for EVM opcodes where each instruction can be inspected and run. Builders use it to learn what an opcode does and to experiment with short sequences of instructions.

name: L2BEAT
description: L2BEAT publishes risk analysis, activity data and research on Ethereum layer 2 networks. Builders use it to compare rollups and check their security assumptions before choosing where to deploy.

name: Certora AutoProver
description: Certora AutoProver is an AI bot that automates parts of formal verification for smart contracts. Verification engineers use it to generate and run checks with less manual specification work.

name: blockaid
description: Blockaid is a closed-source security service that detects malicious activity and is integrated into many wallets and sites. Builders integrate it to simulate a transaction and warn a user before a harmful signature.

name: crossmint
description: Crossmint offers stablecoin APIs aimed at enterprises, including cross-chain flows. Builders use it to add stablecoin payments to an application without building the payment rails.

name: relay
description: Relay is a hosted service for cross-chain routing and transaction execution.

name: flashbots protect
description: Flashbots Protect is an RPC endpoint that keeps transactions out of the public mempool and returns MEV refunds. Wallet and application builders point users at it to reduce frontrunning on their transactions.

name: Across Toolkit
description: The Across toolkit is an SDK for bridging and intent-based transfers through Across. Builders import it to fetch quotes, submit deposits, and move funds between chains from application code.

name: 4byte
description: 4byte.directory is a public registry of function and event signatures keyed by their four-byte selectors. Builders query it to resolve selectors while decoding calldata and unverified contracts.

name: Helios (a16z)
description: Helios from a16z is a portable light client that serves verified Ethereum and other chain data without trusting an RPC provider. Builders run it or embed the Rust library when an application must check the data it receives.

name: multicall.py
description: multicall.py is a Python client that batches many contract calls into a single Multicall aggregate call. Python builders install it to turn hundreds of reads into one RPC request.

name: w3 (Golang JSON-RPC client)
description: w3 is a modular Go JSON-RPC client for Ethereum with first-class ABI support and request batching. Go builders import it when contract calls should be typed and many requests sent in one batch.

name: EVMole
description: EVMole extracts function selectors, arguments, and control flow from raw EVM bytecode, including contracts with no verified source. Builders point it at an unknown contract to work out what its functions take.

name: hardhat-tracer
description: hardhat-tracer is a Hardhat plugin that prints internal calls, events, and storage operations for a transaction in the console. Hardhat users install it to see what actually happened inside a failing test transaction.

name: DAppNode
description: DAppNode is an operating system with an app store for running Ethereum execution and consensus clients and other node software on your own hardware. Someone setting up a home node installs it and picks client packages instead of configuring each service by hand.

name: ethereum-helm-charts
description: ethereum-helm-charts are Helm charts from ethPandaOps for running Ethereum execution and consensus clients and related infrastructure on Kubernetes. Teams add them to a cluster rather than writing client manifests themselves.

name: micro-eth-signer
description: micro-eth-signer is a minimal JavaScript library for building and signing Ethereum transactions, built on the audited noble cryptography libraries by the same author. Builders install it when a small signing dependency matters more than a full client library.

name: Commit-Boost
description: Commit-Boost is a validator sidecar that runs MEV-Boost together with other community-built commitment protocols. Validator operators run it instead of the plain sidecar when they want to take on commitments beyond block sourcing.

name: contender (Flashbots)
description: contender from Flashbots is a load-testing tool that floods EVM execution nodes over JSON-RPC and benchmarks the results. Teams benchmarking a client point it at an endpoint to generate load and measure throughput.

name: mev-boost-relay (Flashbots)
description: mev-boost-relay is the reference relay server for MEV-Boost proposer-builder separation, run by relay operators rather than validators. A team standing up its own relay runs this implementation.

name: rbuilder
description: rbuilder is a Rust MEV-Boost block builder that constructs blocks and submits them to relays. Teams that build blocks run it directly or fork it as the base for their own builder.

name: Checkpointz
description: Checkpointz is a beacon-chain checkpoint sync provider from ethPandaOps. Node operators run one or point a consensus client at an existing instance to bootstrap a node in minutes instead of syncing from genesis.

name: Irys
description: Irys, formerly Bundlr, is a JavaScript SDK for permanent and programmable data storage built on Arweave. Applications install it when data should be paid for once and kept indefinitely.

name: RISC Zero risc0-ethereum
description: risc0-ethereum holds the integration libraries and verifier contracts for using the RISC Zero zkVM with Ethereum and other EVM chains. Teams proving computation off chain import these crates to settle the resulting proofs onchain.

name: SP1 (Succinct)
description: SP1 from Succinct is a zero-knowledge virtual machine that proves correct execution of RISC-V programs, and it is used to generate proofs for rollups and bridges. Teams compile a Rust program with it when a proof must stand in for re-executing that program onchain.

name: Ithaca Account (Porto)
description: Ithaca Account is the set of EIP-7702 smart account contracts behind Porto, an account standard for web authentication and payments. Teams picking an EIP-7702 implementation can read, fork, or deploy these contracts.

name: Base Account SDK
description: Base Account SDK is Coinbase's package for Base Account, a smart-contract wallet with passkey signing and gasless transactions. Web builders install it to add passkey sign-in and sponsored transactions, separate from the older Coinbase Wallet SDK.

name: MetaMask Delegation Framework (Gator)
description: The MetaMask Delegation Framework, known as Gator, is a set of contracts that let one account grant specific revocable permissions to another account or agent along the lines of ERC-7715 and ERC-7710. Teams building delegated or agent-controlled permissions import these contracts and write their own caveat enforcers against them.

name: relayscan
description: relayscan monitors MEV-Boost relays and publishes data on bids, delivered payloads, and relay behavior. Block builders and researchers query its hosted JSON endpoints or run the command line tool against their own data.

name: Elixir Ethers
description: Elixir Ethers is a library for calling and decoding Ethereum smart contracts from Elixir. Builders use it when the backend is written in Elixir, where options are few.

name: essential-eth
description: essential-eth is a lightweight JavaScript client library that bundles to roughly a tenth of the size of ethers.js or web3.js. Builders install it when bundle size on the frontend is the constraint.

name: ethers-kt
description: ethers-kt is an async Kotlin library for interacting with EVM chains, targeting the JVM and Android. Kotlin builders use it to read contracts and send transactions from server or mobile code.

name: ethkit (Sequence)
description: ethkit is a Go toolkit for building Ethereum applications from the team behind the Sequence JavaScript SDK. Go builders import it for wallet handling, ABI work, and RPC calls.

name: js-ethereum-cryptography
description: js-ethereum-cryptography is an audited JavaScript package bundling the hashing and curve primitives that tooling such as ethers.js and web3.js builds on. Builders install it directly when they need keccak, secp256k1, or BIP-39 work without a full client library.

name: ox
description: ox is a low-level TypeScript library of Ethereum primitives covering ABI, RLP, hex, signing, and transactions, and it sits under viem and other wevm tools. Builders import it directly when they want the primitives without the client layer.

name: py_ecc
description: py_ecc is a Python library for elliptic curve pairing operations over bn128 and BLS12-381, used by py-evm and other Python tooling. Builders import it for precompile or BLS work in Python.

name: safe-eth-py
description: safe-eth-py is the Python SDK from the Safe team for building, signing, and relaying Safe multisig transactions. Python builders use it to drive Safe accounts from backend code.

name: WTF Solidity
description: WTF Solidity is a free open-source Solidity course running from basics to advanced topics, with runnable code examples in Chinese and English. Beginners work through it to learn Solidity by editing and running each example.

name: evm-storage
description: evm-storage turns a transaction hash into readable state diffs and can list a contract's full storage. Builders install the command line tool when they need to see exactly which storage slots a call changed.

name: forky
description: forky is a fork choice viewer for the Ethereum beacon chain. Consensus client developers self-host it or use the public instances to see and debug fork choice behavior on mainnet and testnets.

name: geas (Good Ethereum Assembler)
description: geas, the Good Ethereum Assembler, is an assembler for writing raw EVM bytecode by hand, maintained by a go-ethereum core developer. It is used for EIP test cases and other low-level contract work.

name: pyevmasm
description: pyevmasm is a Python disassembler and assembler for EVM bytecode from Trail of Bits. Analysis scripts import it to turn bytecode into instructions and back.

name: revm-inspectors
description: revm-inspectors is a Rust crate of EVM execution hooks and tracing built on revm, and it powers call tracing in Reth and Foundry. Rust builders import it to build their own tracers and debuggers.

name: tracoor
description: tracoor is an explorer for beacon states and execution traces. Client and protocol developers self-host it to inspect block and state traces on devnets and testnets.

name: EthPillar
description: EthPillar is a setup script and terminal interface for installing and managing an Ethereum staking node with execution, consensus and MEV-Boost clients. Solo stakers run it to stand up a node without editing client configuration by hand.

name: scopelint
description: scopelint is an opinionated formatter and linter for Foundry Solidity projects. Builders install it to hold a codebase to the ScopeLift conventions.

name: simple-optimism-node
description: simple-optimism-node is a one-command Docker setup for running an OP Stack node. Builders run it to get their own Optimism node, in the same way eth-docker covers mainnet clients.

name: foundry-toolchain (GitHub Action)
description: foundry-toolchain is the official GitHub Action that installs Foundry in continuous integration. Builders add it to a workflow so forge test and forge script run on every pull request.

name: Rocket Pool Smart Node
description: Rocket Pool Smart Node is the command line package node operators run to set up and manage a Rocket Pool minipool, wrapping execution and consensus clients plus validator duties.

name: Sedge
description: Sedge is a command line setup tool from Nethermind that generates docker-compose configurations for execution, consensus, and validator client combinations. Builders run it to get a working node setup without writing the compose files.

name: c-kzg-4844
description: c-kzg-4844 is the reference C implementation, with Rust bindings, of the KZG polynomial commitment scheme used for EIP-4844 and EIP-7594 blobs, and it is embedded in most execution and consensus clients. Rollup and blob tooling imports the bindings to produce KZG commitments and proofs.

name: nimbus-eth1
description: nimbus-eth1 is an Ethereum execution client built for resource-restricted devices, from the team behind the Nimbus consensus client. Operators run it where memory and storage are tight, separately from nimbus-eth2 on the consensus side.

name: @nomicfoundation/slang
description: slang from the Nomic Foundation is a modular Solidity compiler frontend with a parser, concrete syntax tree, and bindings. Builders import it when writing a linter, formatter, or other tool that has to understand Solidity source.

name: BuildBear
description: BuildBear is a hosted service that spins up a private testnet sandbox mirroring a real chain such as Ethereum, Polygon, BSC, or Arbitrum. Builders point tests at it to work against a private fork with real chain state.

name: builder-playground
description: builder-playground is a self-contained local environment for testing the full block building loop of proposer, relay, and builder on layer 1 and layer 2. It serves the small group working on block building infrastructure.

name: ethereum-genesis-generator
description: ethereum-genesis-generator creates execution and consensus layer genesis state for a testnet and serves it over a web server. Devnet and rollup teams run it to produce the genesis files for a custom network.

name: PoWFaucet
description: PoWFaucet is a modular testnet faucet for EVM chains with anti-abuse methods including a mining puzzle, captcha, IP limits, and Gitcoin Passport, and it backs the Sepolia proof-of-work faucet. Teams running a testnet self-host it to hand out test ETH without giving it all to one address.

name: py-solc-x
description: py-solc-x is a Python wrapper and version manager for the solc Solidity compiler, used by Brownie and Ape style test suites. Python builders install it to fetch and switch compiler versions from their own scripts.

name: spamoor
description: spamoor is a configurable Ethereum transaction generator for load-testing testnets and devnets with realistic traffic. Teams point it at a network to see how it behaves under sustained transaction volume.

name: Stylus SDK (Rust)
description: The Stylus SDK is the Rust SDK for writing smart contracts that run in Arbitrum's Stylus environment alongside the EVM. Rust builders use it when contract logic should be written in Rust rather than Solidity.

name: ant-design-web3
description: ant-design-web3 is a React component library from the Ant Design team for wallet connection and account interfaces. Builders drop it into a React application as an alternative to RainbowKit or ConnectKit.

name: Assertoor
description: Assertoor runs configurable checks and assertions against a live Ethereum devnet to validate its behavior. Client and devnet teams use it to confirm a running network is healthy, in the same family as Hive.

name: goevmlab
description: goevmlab is an EVM fuzzing and differential testing lab built by a go-ethereum core developer. EVM implementers use it to fuzz their own implementation and compare its behavior against others to find divergences.

name: Agora
description: Agora is an onchain governance application used by protocols including Optimism, ENS, and Uniswap to run delegate voting. It is a Next.js application a DAO deploys rather than a library a builder imports.

name: Checkpoint (Snapshot Labs)
description: Checkpoint from Snapshot Labs is a library for indexing Ethereum and Starknet contract events and serving them over GraphQL. Builders install it to turn their own contract events into a GraphQL API, separate from the Snapshot voting application.

name: mempool-dumpster
description: mempool-dumpster continuously records observed mempool transactions into Parquet and CSV files for MEV and mempool research. Researchers pull the hosted dumps from Flashbots or run the Go collector against their own node.

name: xatu
description: xatu is network monitoring tooling with collection clients, called sentries, and a central server that pipelines consensus and execution telemetry. Node and infrastructure teams run it to gather telemetry from their own nodes.

name: Codex
description: Codex is a hosted API with a TypeScript SDK for real-time token prices, holder data, and market data. Builders install it when a trading or portfolio application needs live market data.

name: @ledgerhq/hw-app-eth
description: The Ledger hw-app-eth package is the JavaScript API for signing Ethereum transactions and messages with a Ledger device, and it sits behind the Ledger connectors in wagmi and viem. Wallet and application builders import it to add hardware wallet signing.

name: @noble/secp256k1
description: noble secp256k1 is a standalone pure JavaScript library for secp256k1 signing and ECDH, used by many wallets and libraries. Builders install it on its own when they need signing without the wider noble curves package.

name: blst
description: blst is a multilingual BLS12-381 signature library and the BLS implementation behind most Ethereum consensus clients. Builders link against it in Rust, C, or Go when writing validator or consensus tooling.

name: coins-bip32
description: coins-bip32 is a Rust library for BIP-32 hierarchical deterministic key derivation, used by ethers-rs and other Rust wallets and signers. Rust builders add it when an application derives keys from a seed.

name: eciesjs
description: eciesjs implements the Elliptic Curve Integrated Encryption Scheme for secp256k1 in JavaScript. Builders import it to encrypt and decrypt data against an Ethereum-style keypair.

name: eth-crypto
description: eth-crypto is a set of JavaScript helpers for signing, verifying, recovering addresses, and ECIES encryption alongside ethers or web3. Builders import it for one-off cryptographic steps that the client libraries do not expose directly.

name: k256 (RustCrypto)
description: k256 from RustCrypto is a pure Rust secp256k1 implementation covering ECDSA signing, verification, public key recovery, Schnorr, and ECDH, and it sits under reth, Alloy, and most Rust tooling. Rust builders depend on it directly when they handle signatures themselves.

name: keypo CLI
description: keypo is a local-first command line tool for hardware-bound key management and encrypted secret storage, aimed at AI agents that hold credentials. It installs from a Homebrew tap on macOS.

name: mcl (herumi)
description: mcl from herumi is a portable pairing-based cryptography library used for BLS signature operations by several Ethereum consensus clients. Builders link against it for BLS work in C++ or Go.

name: OKX js-wallet-sdk
description: The OKX js-wallet-sdk is a TypeScript signature SDK covering Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Cosmos, and other chains. Builders install it to derive keys and sign transactions for several chains through one API.

name: Trezor Connect
description: Trezor Connect is a JavaScript SDK for integrating Trezor hardware wallet signing, including Ethereum, into applications and wallets. Builders use it when users should sign with a Trezor device.

name: 1inch AI (MCP + Agent Skills)
description: 1inch AI is the official distribution point for the 1inch hosted MCP server and its agent skills, covering token swaps, limit orders, and SDK documentation search. Agent builders point Claude, Cursor, or Copilot at it so an agent can quote and place swaps.

name: Alchemy MCP Server
description: The Alchemy MCP Server gives AI clients access to Alchemy's blockchain data and RPC APIs across more than 100 chains. The hosted server at mcp.alchemy.com is the maintained route, while the open source repository holds the legacy local version.

name: Coinbase Payments MCP
description: The Coinbase Payments MCP, now documented as the Agentic Wallet MCP, gives an AI agent tools to move and accept crypto payments through Coinbase's payment APIs. Builders add it when an agent needs to send or receive payments.

name: op-rbuilder
description: op-rbuilder is a block builder for OP Stack chains, adapted from rbuilder for rollup sequencer block production. Rollup teams run it as the builder behind their sequencer.

name: rollup-boost
description: rollup-boost is a sidecar for OP Stack sequencers that adds MEV-Boost style external block building to a rollup. Sequencer operators run it when blocks should come from outside builders.

name: DIA Oracles
description: DIA Oracles is an open-source oracle platform that delivers customizable price and data feeds for contracts to read onchain. Contract developers wire its feeds in instead of building their own oracle.

name: Lido Ethereum SDK
description: The Lido Ethereum SDK is the official package for staking and managing stETH and wstETH through the Lido protocol. Builders install it to add staking to an application without writing the Lido contract calls by hand.

name: Machine Payments Protocol SDK (wevm)
description: The Machine Payments Protocol SDK, published as mppx by the wevm team behind viem and wagmi, is a TypeScript implementation of an agent payments specification. Builders install it to let a service or agent pay and charge programmatically.

name: Request Network
description: Request Network is a protocol and JavaScript library for creating, paying, and tracking crypto invoices and payment requests onchain. Builders install the client library to add invoicing to their own application.

name: Stripe Crypto Onramp
description: Stripe Crypto Onramp is an embeddable fiat-to-crypto onramp SDK for web, iOS, Android, and React Native that delivers purchased crypto to a user's wallet. Builders embed it so users can fund a wallet with a card instead of transferring in.

name: x402
description: x402 is an open payments protocol built on the HTTP 402 status code that lets an application or agent pay per request in stablecoins without accounts or API keys. Builders add its middleware to a service to charge per call, or to a client so it can pay.

name: Chainlist
description: Chainlist is a directory of EVM chain IDs and public RPC endpoints that developers and wallets use to add a network. The repository is the source of chainlist.org.

name: Dora the Explorer
description: Dora the Explorer is a lightweight slot-by-slot explorer for the Ethereum beacon chain. Teams running a devnet or testnet deploy it to see consensus activity on their own network.

name: ethereum-lists/chains
description: ethereum-lists/chains is the canonical metadata list for EVM chains, covering chain ID, name, native currency, and RPC URLs. Builders pull chains.json from it to populate wallet and network configuration instead of hardcoding chain data.

name: 1RPC
description: 1RPC from Automata Network is a privacy-preserving public RPC endpoint for Ethereum and other EVM chains. Builders point an application at it when request metadata should not be tied back to users.

name: All That Node
description: All That Node is a multi-chain node-as-a-service platform offering shared and dedicated Ethereum RPC nodes. Builders sign up for an endpoint instead of running their own node.

name: BlockPI Network
description: BlockPI Network is a hosted RPC service for Ethereum and more than 70 other chains, with shared and dedicated node tiers. Builders use it for chain access without operating infrastructure.

name: Chainnodes
description: Chainnodes provides RPC and node infrastructure for Ethereum and the major layer 2 networks, including archival endpoints. Builders buy endpoints there when an application needs historical state as well as current data.

name: enr (Ethereum Node Record)
description: enr is the Rust implementation of EIP-778 Ethereum Node Records, used by discv5 and the consensus and execution peer-to-peer stack. Rust builders add the crate to read and write node records.

name: Lava Network
description: Lava Network is a decentralized RPC access layer that routes requests across independent node operators for Ethereum and more than 27 other chains. Builders route calls through it when access should not depend on one provider.

name: NOWNodes
description: NOWNodes is a node-as-a-service provider covering Ethereum and more than 125 other chains, with shared and dedicated nodes plus block explorers. Builders get an API key for hosted RPC across the chains they support.

name: OnFinality
description: OnFinality offers an RPC API and dedicated node hosting for Ethereum and more than 130 other networks, with indexing add-ons. Builders use it when one provider should cover both node access and indexed data.

name: Validation Cloud
description: Validation Cloud is an enterprise RPC node API for Ethereum and more than 50 protocols, alongside staking and analytics services. Builders pick it when they need support commitments and analytics with the endpoint.

name: Building Secure Contracts
description: Building Secure Contracts is Trail of Bits' collection of guidelines, checklists, and training material for writing and reviewing Solidity contracts. Solidity developers work through its exercises and program analysis tutorials while building and reviewing code.

name: Immunefi
description: Immunefi is a bug bounty platform where projects post rewards for whitehats who find and responsibly disclose contract vulnerabilities. Teams list a program there to give researchers a paid route to report issues.

name: Radar (Auditware)
description: Radar, from Auditware, is a static analysis tool that covers Solidity as well as Rust, Anchor, and Stylus contracts. Auditors run it to get findings across a mixed contract codebase.

name: Slippy
description: Slippy is a Solidity linter for static analysis of smart contracts. Teams install the npm package to lint contracts as part of a build.

name: primitive-types
description: primitive-types provides the shared Rust U256, H160, and H256 types used across Ethereum and Substrate node and tooling codebases. Rust builders add it when their code has to carry Ethereum-sized integers and hashes.

name: ruint
description: ruint is a const-generic unsigned integer type for Rust that represents Ethereum's 256-bit words, and it sits under Alloy and Reth. Rust builders add it directly when they need fixed-width big integers.

name: solidity-docgen
description: solidity-docgen generates Markdown documentation for a Solidity project from its NatSpec comments. Teams run it so published docs stay in step with the contract source.

name: SolidState Solidity
description: SolidState Solidity is an upgradeable-first contract library built around the diamond pattern of EIP-2535. Teams import it when contracts are organized as diamond facets from the start.

name: weiroll
description: weiroll is an operation-chaining scripting language and set of contracts for composing many EVM calls into one transaction. Teams building call-routing or batching systems use it to express the call sequence as a script.

name: eth.limo
description: eth.limo is a gateway that serves ENS-named, IPFS-hosted frontends over ordinary HTTPS, such as yourname.eth.limo. Teams shipping an IPFS frontend point users at their eth.limo address so a normal browser can load it.

name: Pinata
description: Pinata is an IPFS pinning and file upload service used to host NFT metadata and images for contract projects. Teams upload assets there so token metadata stays available after mint.

name: ethr-did-resolver
description: ethr-did-resolver resolves decentralized identifiers anchored to Ethereum addresses. Applications that handle ethr identifiers install it to look up and manage those records.

name: mipd
description: mipd is a set of TypeScript utilities implementing EIP-6963 multi injected provider discovery for detecting installed browser wallets. Builders install it on its own when they need wallet discovery without pulling in wagmi.

name: arkworks algebra
description: arkworks algebra is a set of Rust libraries for finite field, elliptic curve, and polynomial arithmetic, and it is the math layer under many SNARK and STARK toolchains. Rust builders add the ark crates when writing proving code from the ground up.

name: gnark-crypto
description: gnark-crypto provides elliptic curve and pairing cryptography for BN, BLS12, BLS24, and BW6 curves, and it is the backend of the gnark SNARK library. Go builders import it directly for curve and pairing math.

name: Lambdaworks
description: Lambdaworks is a Rust library of SNARK and STARK prover components that can be used piecemeal or assembled into a custom proving system. Teams pull its crates when building their own prover rather than adopting a finished one.

name: op-succinct
description: op-succinct is a proving engine that generates SP1 validity proofs for OP Stack rollups. Rollup teams deploy it to turn an OP Stack chain into a validity proof rollup, running it as a separate service.

name: Plonky3
description: Plonky3 is a toolkit of polynomial IOP building blocks for constructing custom SNARK and STARK proving systems, and several zkVM projects build on it. Rust builders add the p3 crates when writing their own proving system.

name: powdr
description: powdr is a toolkit for accelerating and hardening zkVMs by moving specific computations into custom circuits. Teams running a zkVM use it to generate custom precompiles and check constraints, and its authors still describe the code as experimental.

name: rsp (Succinct)
description: rsp from Succinct generates zero-knowledge proofs of Ethereum and OP Stack block execution, built on Reth. Its authors describe it as a minimal work in progress that is not meant for production, so it mainly serves teams already building on SP1.

name: snark-verifier (Axiom)
description: snark-verifier generates gas-efficient onchain verifiers for halo2 SNARKs and is maintained by Axiom, forked from the original PSE repository. halo2 developers import the crate to produce the Solidity verifier that checks their proofs onchain.

name: web3-ethereum-defi
description: web3-ethereum-defi is a Python library for DeFi integration and data research, with wrappers for Uniswap, Aave, Chainlink, and USDC on top of web3.py. Python builders import it instead of writing those protocol wrappers themselves.

name: Nexth
description: Nexth is a Next.js starter kit wired up with viem, wagmi, Sign-In with Ethereum, and Tailwind. Builders clone it to start from a working frontend rather than assembling the same pieces again.

name: Tenderly CLI
description: The Tenderly CLI is the command line client for Tenderly, pushing contracts for verification and driving error tracking, monitoring, and alerting. Builders install it to run those steps from a terminal or a continuous integration job.

name: rocketh
description: rocketh is a deployment and test harness for Ethereum contracts built around viem, keeping one record of deployments per network so scripts and tests agree. Builders use it when they want repeatable deployments without Hardhat, which the hardhat-deploy plugin wraps over the same code.

name: headlong
description: headlong is a Java library for encoding and decoding contract ABI calldata and RLP, tuned for throughput in JVM services. Java builders add it when a backend has to process a high volume of Ethereum calls.

name: sol-profiler
description: sol-profiler is a command line tool that lists a Solidity contract's methods with their visibility, mutability and modifiers. Reviewers run it to see the surface of a contract at a glance.

name: Delphereum
description: Delphereum is a web3 implementation for Delphi that lets Object Pascal desktop and mobile applications sign transactions and read contract state. It is the maintained route to Ethereum for builders working in that language.

name: web3dart
description: web3dart is an Ethereum client library for Dart and Flutter covering JSON-RPC calls, contract bindings, and local transaction signing. Flutter builders use it as the general client for mobile applications.

name: Ethereumex
description: Ethereumex is an Elixir JSON-RPC client for Ethereum and the transport layer that higher-level libraries such as Elixir Ethers build on. Elixir builders configure it by name even when they work through a higher-level library.

name: hs-web3
description: hs-web3 is a Haskell library for talking to Ethereum nodes, with contract ABI code generation through Template Haskell. It is the route to Ethereum for builders working in Haskell.

name: ethereal
description: ethereal is a Go command line tool for everyday Ethereum tasks, including sending transactions, managing ENS records, transferring tokens, and inspecting accounts. Builders install it for one-off operations that do not justify a script.

name: rust-web3
description: rust-web3 is a Rust implementation of the web3 JSON-RPC client with pluggable transports. It predates Alloy and carries no deprecation notice.

name: Solidity by Example
description: Solidity by Example is a collection of short annotated Solidity snippets organized by language feature and pattern. Builders look things up there while writing contracts.

name: EVMConnector
description: EVMConnector is a browser workspace for calling contract functions on any EVM chain, with saved contracts and shareable call links. Builders use it to drive a contract without writing a script.

name: One Click Dapp
description: One Click Dapp generates a hosted web interface for a deployed contract from its ABI and address. Builders use it to give a contract a usable interface without writing frontend code.

name: Web3Client
description: Web3Client is a browser tool for creating, testing, and sharing contract ABIs and the calls made against them. Builders use it to work out a call and hand the result to someone else.

name: SmartContractGUI
description: SmartContractGUI turns an uploaded ABI into an interface for reading from and writing to that contract on any EVM chain. Builders use it when they have an ABI but no frontend.

name: ABI Calldata Layout Visualizer
description: The ABI Calldata Layout Visualizer decodes ABI calldata and draws its byte layout, showing where heads, tails, and offsets sit in the encoded payload. Builders open it when a plain decoder does not explain why an encoding is wrong.

name: HashEx ABI Encoder
description: The HashEx ABI Encoder is a web form that ABI-encodes constructor and function arguments from a pasted signature and values. Builders use it when they need encoded arguments and are not at a terminal.

name: Chainlink Faucets
description: Chainlink Faucets dispense testnet ETH and LINK across the supported test networks. Builders use them to fund an account before deploying and testing contracts on a testnet.

name: Pessimistic Spotter
description: Pessimistic Spotter monitors deployed contracts for exploit patterns and raises alerts. Teams point it at their own contracts to catch an attack while it is still running.

name: Kaleido
description: Kaleido is a hosted platform for running permissioned and public chain environments, including managed Ethereum nodes and tokenization services.

name: Watchdata
description: Watchdata provides hosted blockchain APIs and RPC endpoints across several networks, including Ethereum mainnet and testnets. Builders use it as a hosted endpoint when they do not run their own node.

name: InfStones
description: InfStones offers managed node infrastructure with RPC APIs, non-custodial staking, and node monitoring across many chains. Builders use it instead of operating their own nodes.

name: Tatum
description: Tatum is a TypeScript SDK over its hosted RPC and blockchain APIs, covering wallets, transactions, tokens, and notifications. Builders install it when one package should cover both chain access and wallet operations.

name: Amberdata
description: Amberdata is a commercial digital asset data platform covering onchain, market, and DeFi datasets through APIs aimed at financial institutions. Builders call it when an application needs market and protocol data from one vendor.

name: Aleph Cloud
description: Aleph Cloud is a decentralized cloud offering storage, virtual machines, and hosting that contracts and applications can reach as an off-chain data layer. Builders deploy onto it when application data and compute should not sit with a single hosting provider.

name: eth-prices
description: eth-prices is a Rust crate that estimates the price of an Ethereum asset by reading Uniswap V2 and V3 pools and ERC-4626 vaults through an RPC provider, with no exchange rate API involved. Rust builders add it when a price should be derived from onchain liquidity rather than read from an oracle feed.
